title: Counter loop escape segment
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, distinct states $a$ and $ex$, and let $e:\\{0,1\\}\\hookrightarrow\\Gamma$ encode Boolean symbols. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with the encoded word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. For an initial configuration $c$, a run-length function $\\tau$, and a property $P$ of the first $k$ work-head positions, choose $r_0$ strictly below the binary value of $w$. Suppose each round $r\\le r_0$ satisfies the round conditions for exit set $\\{some\\ ex\\}$ and property $P$, and the configuration after round $r_0$ is in state $ex$. Then the counter-loop machine reaches its escape configuration after $\\sum_{r\\le r_0}\\tau(c_r)+\\operatorname{overhead}(w,r_0+1)$ steps, where $c_r$ is the $r$th round configuration; its extra tape on the word cells agrees with the encoded counter word after $r_0+1$ decrements. Before that time its state is neither done nor escape. Throughout the segment the extra head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and $P$ holds for the first $k$ head positions at every time through the endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: Counter word $w$ and index $r_0$ strictly below its binary value
Initial extra-tape buffer agreement for all $-1\\le p\\le |w|$
Every round $r\\le r_0$ satisfies the round conditions
The configuration after round $r_0$ has state $ex$
